title: November FIDE Rating List: Nihal Enters Top 20, Sindarov Leads Gukesh By 72 Points
summary: GM Javokhir Sindarov goes into the 2026 Salesforce FIDE World Championship against reigning champion GM Gukesh Dommaraju with a lead of 72 rating points and 22 places on the November FIDE rating list. The biggest climber near the top of the list was GM Nihal Sarin, whose 2859 performance in the European Club Cup took him up to a career-best world number-19, while a casualty was GM Hans Niemann, who dropped out of the 2700 club after a disappointing U.S. Championship. The women's top-10 rankings stayed unchanged, but the U.S. Women's Championship caused wild swings—IM Alice Lee climbed to 14th and took over as the U.S. women's number-one, IM Carissa Yip dropped 31 points, while winner WIM Rachael Li climbed 50 points. The standout women's performance, however, was by FM Bodhana Sivanandan, who earned the international master title and is the seventh youngest IM, male or female, of all time. Despite a number of top players being in action in October, the rankings at the top were left almost unchanged—GM Wei Yi edged above GM Vincent Keymer into eighth place after a strong showing in the European Club Cup, but has since dipped below the German number-one after three draws in the Chinese League. title: Carlsen Trains With Abdusattorov In Spain Ahead Of Total Chess Debut
summary: GM Magnus Carlsen and GM Nodirbek Abdusattorov have teamed up for a training camp in Spain ahead of the Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot. Joining them are GM David Howell and Carlsen's longtime coach, GM Peter Heine Nielsen. Carlsen and Abdusattorov will be among 24 players competing in Budapest on November 10–20, testing a format combining fast classical, rapid, and blitz. The tournament is a trial run for the FIDE-approved tour, which launches in 2027 and will crown a World Combined Champion. On Saturday, a post shared on Carlsen’s social media accounts offered a glimpse of the preparations at his holiday home in Spain. The post includes three images that include Howell and Nielsen, along with a video of the two top-10 stars playing blitz together. "Someone brought a chess board into this house," the caption reads.

title: KazChess Masters: Dubov moves ahead with consecutive wins
summary:
Vokhidov and Lazavik trail by half a point

Daniil Dubov has taken the sole lead at the KazChess Masters in Almaty after scoring consecutive victories in rounds five and six. The Russian grandmaster has collected 4½ points from 6 games and stands half a point ahead of Shamsiddin Vokhidov and Denis Lazavik.

The tournament had initially been led by the Kazakh duo of Edgar Mamedov and Denis Makhnev, who both reached 2½/3 . In Thursday's fourth round, however, Lazavik joined them at the top of the standings by defeating Vokhidov. Co-leaders Mamedov and Makhnev both drew their games, while 14-year-old Mark Smirnov scored his second consecutive victory, this time against Sauat Nurgaliyev.

Rounds five and six brought an unusual coincidence. Both days featured three decisive games, and the winners were exactly the same: the tournament's three highest-rated participants, Mahammad Muradli (2662), Dubov (2654) and Vokhidov (2649).

Round 5 results

Round 6 results

Shamsiddin Vokhidov | Photo: Nils Rohde / ChessBase

Their routes of the three top seeds to the consecutive victories had been rather different. Muradli had started with two losses and two draws, so his back-to-back wins allowed him to return to a fifty-percent score. Dubov, meanwhile, had collected one win and three draws before his latest successes, which have taken him to an undefeated 4½/6. Vokhidov had a more uneven start, with two wins, a draw and a loss, and has now climbed to 4/6.

Lazavik is the only player other than Dubov to remain undefeated, drawing his games in rounds five and six. The Belarusian GM is now tied for second place with Vokhidov. The early co-leaders Mamedov and Makhnev, meanwhile, have both suffered their first defeats and now stand on 3½/6, one point behind Dubov.

Sunday's seventh round will see all three frontrunners playing with the black pieces. With three rounds remaining, Dubov has a narrow advantage, while the two Kazakh players who set the early pace remain within striking distance.
